# Feature: Fixed world scale with camera

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

One fixed world scale for every level, set by the movement-room reference, so tiles and Jolly render the same size and undistorted whether the level is a small room or a large scrolling one. The camera/scroll work changed how the board is fitted to the screen and coupled the HUD into that fit; the GUI was fine before the camera, so this feature leaves HUD sizing exactly as it was and fixes only the world/board scale.

## User Story

As a player, I want every level to draw its tiles and Jolly at the same size and shape, so that moving between rooms (movement-room, scroll-room, warp-end-room, chip1) never makes the world grow, shrink, or stretch.

## High-Level Use Case

1. Player opens any level. 2. The board is drawn at the fixed world scale (movement-room's on-screen tile size at the same window/canvas size). 3. In a level larger than the viewport the camera scrolls, so more/fewer tiles are visible but each tile is the same number of screen pixels as in movement-room. 4. In a small level the leftover space is letterbox/empty board area, not a zoom-in. 5. The HUD column looks exactly as it did before the camera feature.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the same window/canvas size, when any level loads, then one tile measures the same screen pixels (within rounding) in movement-room, scroll-room, warp-end-room and chip1, in embed and non-embed modes.
- Given a level larger than the viewport, when the player moves, then the camera scrolls as today (GameCamera behaviour unchanged) and tile size does not change while scrolling.
- Given a level smaller than the viewport, when it loads, then it is centred/letterboxed at the fixed scale and is not scaled up to fill the screen (today warp-end-room's 11x7 tiles render much larger than scroll-room's).
- Given any level, when Jolly is drawn, then the sprite keeps its source aspect ratio (square tile, no horizontal/vertical stretch) at rest and while the camera moves.
- The world scale does not come from the level file: every level in levels/ declares tile:64 today, and the renderer must give the same on-screen size even if a level's tile value differed (one renderer-owned world-scale constant, movement-room as reference).

## Edge Cases & Rules

- Window resized: board refits by showing the same fixed-scale tiles letterboxed; tiles must not be non-uniformly stretched to fill, and tile width must equal tile height after resize.
- Scrolling at level edges: camera clamping is unchanged; no scale change at edges.
- Embed and non-embed modes must agree on the fixed scale rule.
- Levels at/under the viewport render as before the camera feature, except at the fixed scale.
- Determinism: renderer-only change; game state, sessions and replay are unaffected.

## UI / Feedback

- HUD/GUI: unchanged. Do not resize, rescale or re-layout the HUD column to make the board fit (it was fine before the camera); hudScale/layoutHud behaviour stays as-is and board fitting must not depend on HUD size, nor HUD on the board's visible-tile count.
- Board area outside a small level is the existing dark background (letterbox), centred.

## Assets & Level Data Needed

- Sprites: none new. Existing 512x512 sprites (incl. jolly.png) are drawn into one fixed square tile.
- Level JSON: no new fields; the renderer ignores per-level variance for on-screen scale (levels/*.json all declare tile:64 today).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On-screen tile size (measured in screen px, same window size) matches movement-room's in scroll-room, warp-end-room and chip1, embed and non-embed.
- [ ] Tiles are square on screen and Jolly is undistorted (sprite aspect = source aspect) in all four levels, including mid-scroll and after a window resize.
- [ ] Camera scrolling still works on scroll-room (camera follows player, clamps at edges) with no scale change while scrolling.
- [ ] HUD column renders identically to before this feature (same size/layout at the same window size); no HUD code changes were needed to achieve the board scale.
- [ ] Existing tests pass, plus a new scale test that pins the fixed tile size across levels of different sizes.

## Out of Scope

- Changing HUD/GUI layout, size or art.
- Changing camera following/clamping behaviour, viewport tile counts as a design choice beyond what the fixed scale implies, level data, movement or any game mechanic.
- Zoom controls or player-adjustable scale.

## Open Questions

- Is movement-room's current on-screen tile size in embed mode the reference, or its non-embed 64px tile? Implementer to pin one, state it in the first task, and keep it identical everywhere. Default assumption: movement-room as it renders today, unchanged.

## Testing

Mechanics playground: reuse movement-room (reference), scroll-room (scrolling), warp-end-room (small room that zooms today) and chip1. Check: screenshot each at the same window size and measure a tile and Jolly; scroll scroll-room end to end; resize the window and re-measure. Record play sessions for replay: no - renderer-only, screenshots + measurements are the evidence.

## Tasks

### fixed-world-scale/pin-world-scale — Pin one renderer-owned world scale from movement-room

- Status: `completed` · Priority: `high` · Kind: `work`
- Description: Replace the per-level fit (fit = min(availW/(VIEW.w*TILE), availH/(VIEW.h*TILE)) in fitBoard, and the VIEW-sized canvas in non-embed) with one fixed on-screen tile size taken from movement-room's current rendering. Small levels letterbox instead of zooming; the camera only changes which tiles are visible. State the pinned reference (embed vs 64px non-embed) in the commit.
- Acceptance: At the same window size, a tile measures the same screen px in movement-room, scroll-room, warp-end-room and chip1; screenshots of all four attached.

### fixed-world-scale/review-fixes-1 — Keep Jolly in frame: camera view = tiles visible at fixed scale

- Status: `completed` · Priority: `high` · Kind: `review-fixes`
- Description: Human playtest (scroll-room): Jolly can go out of frame and not be seen. Cause: camera frames the old 17x16 MAX view, which at the fixed 64px tile is 1088x1024 - taller than the window - so when the camera clamps at the level's top/bottom edges the player is in the cropped part of the view. Fix: in embed, the camera view is the tiles actually visible at 64px in the available area (floor(avail/64), capped by MAX view and level size); board transform centres that view. Tile size unchanged; HUD unchanged.
- Acceptance: In scroll-room at 1280x800 embed, driving Jolly to all four edges/corners keeps the full player tile on screen; same at a smaller window. Tests pin visible-view + player-on-screen for all positions.
- Evidence: `screenshots/features/fixed-world-scale/20261031-153432-scroll-room-bottom-edge.png`
- Evidence: `screenshots/features/fixed-world-scale/20261031-153432-scroll-room-bottom-right.png`
